html:
The constitution of the First Philippine Republic, approved in January 1899 in the town of Malolos. It was the first republican constitution in Asia.

The Philippine Revolution against Spain had flared again in 1898, during the war between Spain and the United States. Revolutionary leader Emilio Aguinaldo declared independence in June 1898 and called a congress of delegates to Malolos, north of Manila. A lawyer, Felipe Calderón, wrote the main draft.

The text set up a republic with a strong elected assembly, a bill of rights, and the separation of church and state, a sharp break after three centuries of rule by friars. Aguinaldo became president when the republic was proclaimed two days later.

It never governed in peace. Spain had already sold the islands to the United States, and in February 1899 the Philippine American War began. Aguinaldo was captured in 1901 and the republic ended. The constitution remains a founding text of Filipino nationalism and the ideals of José Rizal's generation.
sum: The constitution of the First Philippine Republic, approved in January 1899 in the town of Malolos. It was the first republican constitution in Asia.
